properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Ovens River Downstream of Rocky Point.

Minor Flooding Possible along the Ovens river at Wangaratta Monday Afternoon.

The flood peak is now downstream of Docker Road Bridge where minor flooding has eased and is approaching Wangaratta where the peak is possible Monday afternoon.

Minor flooding is possible along the Ovens River around Wangaratta. The Ovens River at Wangaratta is currently at 11.77 metres and rising. The Ovens River at Wangaratta may peak near the minor flood level (11.90 m) Monday afternoon.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams. 
  • Caravan parks and camping grounds may be flooded.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 08/09/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge.

Minor Flooding occurring along the Kiewa at Bandiana and at Kiewa

Moderate to heavy rainfall observed across the Kiewa River catchment since Friday and during the weekend has caused river level rises and minor flooding.

No further significant rainfall is forecast for the next few days.

Minor flooding is occurring along the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge. The Kiewa River at Kiewa (Main Stream) is currently peaking around 3.38 metres. The Kiewa River at Kiewa (Main Stream) is likely to remain above the minor flood level (3.30 m) for the next few days.

The Kiewa River at Bandiana peaked at 2.96 m around 09:30 am Sunday, with minor flooding. The river is currently at 2.91 metres and steady. The Kiewa River at Bandiana is likely to remain above the minor flood level (2.80 m) for the next few days.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

MINOR FLOODING OCCURRING AT BARHAM

The main flood peak along the Murray River has now passed Barham, where minor flooding continues and river levels are slowly falling.   

Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham: 
  • Minor flooding is occurring along the Murray River at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.59 metres and falling slowly, with minor flooding. 
The Murray River at Barham may fall below the minor flood level (5.50 m) overnight Monday into Tuesday.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/(https://www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/)
For emergency assistance call SES on telephone number 132 500. In life-threatening emergencies, call 000 (triplezero) immediately.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 09/09/2026 02:00 pm or as the situation changes.

  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226

properties.location: King River at Docker Road bridge
properties.webBody:
This is a Final Minor Flood Warning for King River. 

Minor flooding is estimated to have eased along the King River

The flood peak is now downstream of Docker Road Bridge where minor flooding has eased and is approaching Wangaratta where the peak is possible Monday afternoon.

No recent observations are available for the King River at Docker Rd Bridge. The river is estimated to have fallen below the minor flood level. The King River at Docker Rd Bridge is expected to remain below the minor flood level (3.70 m).
The threat of flooding is reduced. Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and beware of hazards remaining in the warning area.
What you should do:
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
If your home or business has been flooded:
  • Check for building damage before you enter.
  • Have all electrical and gas equipment professionally tested before use.
  • Clean and dry out the building as soon as possible.
Call Triple Zero (000) in a life threatening emergency. For emergency assistance from the SES call 132 500.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Damage to roads and buildings caused by flooding may still exist in your area. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This will be the last warning for this flood. 

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.

  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.
